overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an inaccurate start time on the website and by not announcing whether it would reconvene before entering executive session; other allegations were not sustained, and the matter was closed after remedial steps.

allegations.summary: Alleged the meeting notice posted on the town website gave an inaccurate start time for the September 29, 2010 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: While we have no reason to believe that the inconsistency was anything more than a clerical error, it is nonetheless a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board deliberated and voted on a letter barring an individual from town offices, a topic not listed in the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Although we are constrained to find that the Board acted within the letter of the Open Meeting Law because the topic was not anticipated in advance of the meeting, the Board failed to act within the spirit of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Alleged the generic notice for the executive session on complaints against a public officer lacked adequate detail.
allegations.key_passage: However, the meeting notice complied with the letter of the Open Meeting Law because it stated the reason for the anticipated executive session, while balancing the privacy rights of the individual who was the subject of the complaint.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board entered executive session on a complaint against an official without 48-hour notice to that individual and denied him a right to be heard in open session.
allegations.key_passage: However, we decline to find that the Board violated the rights of any individual by entering into executive session, as the complainant alleges, because the Chair of the Board did not anticipate that the Chief of Police, who is not a member of the Board, would raise the question of whether the Board wanted to pursue a criminal complaint against a sitting town official.

allegations.summary: Found during review: the Board did not announce before entering executive session whether it would reconvene in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board did not announce whether it would reconvene in open session prior to entering executive session.

remedy: Immediately and in the future comply with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§18-25, and the Open Meeting Law regulations, 940 CMR 29.00.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to immediately and in the future comply with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§18-25, and the Open Meeting Law regulations, 940 CMR 29.00.
